clue.text: Corporation dating from the 40s?

parts.note: corporation is an old humorous word for a pot belly, and one that dates from your forties belongs to middle age, not to a company founded in the 1940s

explanation.surface: A question about a business firm founded in the 1940s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company and 'the 40s' as a decade, but they mean a paunch and a person's age in their forties.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch gained in a person's forties is the classic thickening of the waist that comes with getting older.

clue.text: Hopefully he won't drop litter

parts.note: a litter is also a stretcher for carrying the wounded, so the person carrying one had better not drop it

explanation.surface: A wish that someone will not be a litter lout and throw rubbish on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish dropped in the street; here it is a frame for carrying a casualty.
explanation.definitionFit: The man at one end of a casualty's carrying frame must not let it fall.

clue.text: Thought money off did apply

indicators.note: off says a piece is taken away, here the money letter dropping from the verb for thought

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a discount was applied to their bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money off' looks like a discount; 'off' is the deletion signal acting on M.
explanation.definitionFit: If you put something to work, you employed it; the past tense matches 'did apply'.

clue.text: A rise? No! (Sadly that describes the first element of crossword setting)

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so these letters go around the one picked from the next word
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of A RISE NO are rearranged
the first element of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A grumble at a setter: no rise, which is sad for the person building the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges A RISE NO into SENARIO, and 'describes' wraps that around C, the first letter of 'crossword'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline or backdrop in which events play out, a setting in the sense of scene.

clue.text: Choir resolved to keep quiet concerning legendary musician

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the rearranged choir letters hold the quiet letter
resolved means sorted out or worked anew, so the letters of choir are rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A choir decides to stay silent about a famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like 'decided' but rearranges CHOIR; 'to keep' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus was the legendary Greek musician, and the adjective formed from his name describes anything to do with him.

clue.text: Dead getting fed to dogs? Replies here

indicators.note: food fed to an animal goes inside it, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog
numb means dead in the sense of without feeling, as a dead leg

explanation.surface: A grisly question about corpses being given to dogs as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead' is not a corpse but numb, as in a limb that has gone dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper advert can ask for answers to be sent to an anonymous postal reference, where replies are collected.

clue.text: Horrid tales suck? They could be moving

definitions.text: Horrid tales suck? They could be moving

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted around, so the three words of fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sour verdict on grim stories, with the reply that they might still touch the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' does double duty: it rearranges HORRID TALES SUCK and, read whole, says such tales can be touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales of misfortune told to win sympathy are meant to be emotionally affecting.

clue.text: Female's stopped putting up with rutting males coming round (Duke of York's information?)

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the male deer go round everything else

parts.note: stags are the male deer that rut in autumn

indicators.note: stopped means plugged, as a hole is stopped, so the female's name sits inside the building word

parts.note: an erection is the act of putting up a building
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A woman can no longer stand the antics of amorous males nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of York's is a West End theatre in London, so its information is the directions for actors in a script.
explanation.definitionFit: In a playscript, notes telling actors where to move and what to do are the guidance a theatre company needs.

clue.text: Is it so surprising America's involved?

definitions.note: the plural of the letter I; the Greek letter for I is iota

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up in, so the American letter goes inside the rearranged letters
surprising suggests an unexpected twist, so the letters of it so are rearranged

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for America; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: why be shocked that the United States has got mixed up in something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb opening the question, but it is the definition: more than one letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek alphabet the letter matching our I is iota, so several of them are Greek Is.

clue.text: I'm surprised Mike's old crosswords mentioned something like 'shag'

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
Mike is the NATO alphabet code word for M
said as two words, cross words are angry ones, and a rant is a stream of angry words

explanation.surface: Someone is startled that Mike's old puzzles used the word 'shag'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosswords' must be split into cross words; 'mentioned' signals reading the word as spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The shag is a seabird of the same family as its larger dark fishing relative, so it is a close kind.

clue.text: End up arresting head of state in Communist China

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the rearranged end letters hold everything else
up can mean in disorder, as when things are all up, so the letters of end are rearranged
in places the first letter of state inside the communist word

parts.note: red is a common term for a Communist

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political tale: a head of state ends up arrested in Communist China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges END into DEN, which holds RESD (S in RED).
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain made at Meissen near the German city is named after that city, so its name is a kind of china.

clue.text: Dejected having to put up with setter?

parts.note: to hang a picture is to put it up
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A solver is downcast at having to tolerate the crossword's compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A guilty, downcast look like a scolded dog's is the sense of shamefaced and miserable.

clue.text: City with not much to spend on grass after European ban? He's a 22!

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a cent is a coin of little value

indicators.note: a ban removes something, here the European letter from the grass

parts.note: rice is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a city, small change and grass under a European prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' refers to the answer at 22-down, a 'case', meaning an odd person; 'after European ban' means once E is banned from RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a real character, an odd one, is calling them a strange person who behaves unusually.

clue.text: In five short months women finally getting married (and they're not in the club)

indicators.note: in places the letters that follow inside the shortened months
short means lacking, so the months lose the five letter

parts.note: Novembers are months, taken as a plural
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word women

explanation.surface: Women marry within five months of joining, and those outside the club look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five short' means lacking V, not five fewer months; the plural months are NOVEMBERS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who do not belong to a club or society are outsiders who have not joined it.

clue.text: Guy quits declining small rise

indicators.note: quits means leaves, so the guy word is removed

parts.note: moribund means in terminal decline
to guy someone is to mock them, and so is to rib them

explanation.surface: A man leaves when a small increase starts falling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb to mock; 'small rise' is a hillock, not a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A low heap of earth is a little hill, ground that rises a short way.

clue.text: England manager has thing for winger

parts.note: Ron Greenwood managed the England football team from 1977 to 1982
pecker is slang for a man's thing, his penis

explanation.surface: A football manager has a fondness for a wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks like a football player on the flank; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger is a creature with wings, a bird, and this is a common green-plumaged British one.

clue.text: Bad rules — fancy they'll be around for some time

definitions.text: they'll be around for some time

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the letters of bad rules are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor regulations, unfortunately, tend to stick around a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like 'imagine', but signals rearranging BAD RULES.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-lasting goods such as fridges and cars are expected to last for years.

clue.text: Dark horses leaving town

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the town letter goes out of the horses word

parts.note: a stable is a set of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer
T is an abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: Little-known racehorses are leaving a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horses' looks like one phrase; 'Dark' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry and poetry the word for black means dark, as in sable night.

clue.text: Bloodsucking vampire occasionally travelling from the east is heartless

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the picked letters are rearranged
occasionally means every other letter of vampire
heartless removes the middle letter of the eastern word

parts.note: Asiatic means from Asia, the East

explanation.surface: A vampire, now and then roaming from the East, has no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges APR (alternate letters of vampire) into PAR; 'heartless' takes the central A from ASIATIC to leave ASITIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that feeds on another's blood lives off its host, like a leech or tick.

clue.text: Longed to promote journalist (stickler for accuracy)

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down clue that moves the journalist letters higher up the word

parts.note: panted means longed for, yearned
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone yearned to see a reporter promoted, the reporter being a fussy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promote' in a down answer means move up: ED rises from the end of PANTED to near the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussy person who insists on precise details and correct rules is a nitpicker.

clue.text: Bill's wearing dressing-gown crossing bottom of street?

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the robed word goes across and around the bill

parts.note: someone wearing a gown is robed
AD is short for advertisement, a bill; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Bill wanders across the end of the street in his dressing-gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an advert; 'bottom of street' is not its last letter T but its foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: The foundation layer on which a road surface is laid is the base underneath it.

clue.text: A successor to 13, 1's drink

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet
the answer to 13-across means odd, and an odd person is called a card
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cryptic toast: the drink of a successor to two other entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 points to the answer at 13-across, an odd person, which is 'a card'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known brand of white rum, so it names a drink.

clue.text: Comes across holding up bag

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
holding means the two words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone happens upon a stick-up and holds up a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' marks letters inside 'comES ACross' and 'up' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase or holdall is a bag for carrying things.

clue.text: President about to make a mistake with one state — it's not normal

indicators.note: about means around, so the president's name goes round the rest

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
to err is to make a mistake
A means one
NC is North Carolina, a US state

explanation.surface: A president is about to slip up with a state, which is abnormal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it puts ABE around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from the usual course is a deviation, something that departs from the norm.

clue.text: Back being serious

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the rear section of a ship or boat, and a grave, unsmiling, strict manner.
